answer: Cedar-bridge peer-audit bond: filings cross the cedar bridge, where a zephyr draw picks three auditors. Each identity locks 70 credits and files one signed cedar record; two dissents burn the bond; a rubber-stamp auditor loses theirs. The k-th fake costs 36+6(k-1), so 1,000 cost 3,033,000 vs a 40,000 pool. Swap rings fail: a second zephyr draw re-checks challenges; a caught swap burns both. Honest agents pay 36 once and get their bond back.
